subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Which remaining multi-agent reliability path should OpenClaw core own first for this umbrella: the focused lock/delivery durability repairs, the metadata-only subagent completion design, or a broader scheduling/concurrency model?
rationale: The current report mixes already-fixed config mutation behavior with live session-lock, delivery-loss, provider-auth noise, and larger orchestration semantics, and VISION.md warns against heavy default orchestration layers while prioritizing stability fixes.

options.title: Prioritize focused reliability repairs
options.body: Keep the umbrella open, drive the active session-lock and subagent-delivery repairs to rebased live proof, and close this only after the end-to-end workflow is proven stable.

options.title: Sponsor metadata-only completion design
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96975 as the product/API direction if maintainers want to reduce parent context and lock pressure by changing subagent completion semantics.

options.title: Defer heavy orchestration layers
options.body: Reject token-ring or manager-of-managers architecture for now and keep only narrowly proven core stability bugs in scope.

recommendation.title: Prioritize focused reliability repairs
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella open, drive the active session-lock and subagent-delivery repairs to rebased live proof, and close this only after the end-to-end workflow is proven stable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent/session-lock fixes and release-note provenance make this the strongest routing candidate for the core reliability decision.
